body: I think its fine for a major compatability break (godot 5), but for now i think its to much breakage. Maybe create a [gip?](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals)

Thanks! Maybe I it's worth writing a proposal to ask people to try out a contact bias of 0.2 in their games. 

I traced the bias setting back further and it has been 0.8 for a long time, so probably not an accident, but that doesn't mean it is good or right.

My ambitions for 5.0 would involve getting rid of bias altogether and updating to modern parameters as an absolute minimum. See this modernisation proposal for 3D physics:

[Unify Joint3D spring parameters and make them understandable #14845](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/14845)

So if this is a 5.0 thing, then I don't think it makes any sense. We should have eliminated bias altogether by then.

> However given that this PR is auto-marked as a breaking change

What do you mean "auto-marked"?
Right, sorry, thought it was automatically marked breaking  because of the failed test. My mistake. Edited my comment above to remove that.

Just to clarify here: changing any default value is considered a pretty significant compatibility breakage as anyone using the old default value will have their value changed without notice, as default values are not stored and a missing value is treated as the default, even if it was assigned explicitly to be the default value (and not just left alone, though if the behavior changes that is also a problem), and the change in behavior of the default value itself is breaking

This would need either an issue describing a bug caused by this, or a feature proposal discussing the need for it as an improvement, with clear details on why this is needed

Please try to make any such description as brief and clear as possible, as the long comment above is not very easy to parse so it is hard to understand the justification for this

Breaking compatibility is not completely out of the picture assuming it is sufficiently justified, but that normally requires that the existing behavior is entirely or mostly broken

Thanks. That makes a lot of sense about default values and I really appreciate your time on this. 

I was going to say that I don't think there is justification for the risk, and I should close this PR. but I have come back to edit my comment after finishing work on another test (which better demonstrates the problem). 

So yeah, I will try to put an issue up with a video, and a quick proposal, and let everyone decide if it is a bug they want to fix or not. 

More important than changing bias however, is deprecating bias, and that starts with better testing, and work on modern solvers (I think). 

Also, I added the comment below to the docs, which may be enough to deal with the issue:

[Physics troubleshooting comment](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.6/tutorials/physics/troubleshooting_physics_issues.html)

Issue below created, to aid discussion
[2D Physics collision solver is explosive under pressure #119962](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/119962)

I just want to point out that instead of changing the default value (which breaks compatibility), the project setting can be set to a new ("new default") value only for newly created projects (without breaking compatibility), as was done to set the 3D physics engine to Jolt in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/105737:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d569fcf207aea355ea9d0822255ad490945f5572/editor/editor_node.cpp#L8351

I just pushed the method rburing suggested (thanks). 

Less risk this way, as it can't hurt existing projects. Still debatable for new projects.
